Tuga A6 vs Tuga A8

Buy the Tuga A8 at £379 if you fill in forms, read drawings or want a van mount; buy the Tuga A6 at £349 if you scan barcodes or want the device in a pocket. Both are rugged Android devices for sole traders and small firms, and £30 is too small a gap to decide on.

Verdict

The short answer

The A6 costs £349 and the A8 £379, a gap of £30, so price does not settle this one. They are different shapes of device for different work. Both are rugged Android devices on the same MediaTek Helio P35 processor, both are sealed to IP67, both have a removable battery, and both have dual SIM 4G, NFC and GPS. The decision comes down to two things: whether you scan barcodes, and whether you want to carry a tablet at all.

If you do not scan and do not need a pocket device, the A8 gives you more for £30. Its 8 inch screen against 6 helps with test schedules, long checklists and PDF drawings, and it is rated at 1000 nits, where the A6 lists no brightness figure. The A6's 2160 x 1080 screen is sharper than the A8's 1280 x 800, but on a bright day the brightness figure is the one that counts. The A8 has an 8000mAh battery against 5050mAh, both removable, and 6GB of RAM and 128GB of storage against 4GB and 64GB. It also has VESA mount points and pogo pin contacts, and the £109 Vehicle Mounting Dock is listed for the A8 and not the A6. The A8 does not list a weight, but an 8 inch tablet suits a bag or a van door pocket better than a trouser pocket.

Buy the A6 if you scan or work from a pocket. It has a Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, which the A8 does not have, a 1.5 metre drop rating where the A8 lists none, and a listed operating range of -20°C to 50°C where the A8 lists none. It also runs Android 15 against the A8's Android 12, which matters if your apps need a recent Android version, so check your apps on whichever you choose. Both include 12 months, and both can take the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65. See the electricians page and the field service page, or tell us what you fill in on site and we will say which we would buy.

Choose the Tuga A6 if

  • You scan parcels, stock or asset tags: the A6 has a Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys, and the A8 has no scanner.
  • You want one device that goes in a pocket or a Belt Holster (£22) rather than a tablet in a bag: the A6 weighs 277g, and the Belt Holster is not listed for the A8.
  • Your day is photos, job sheets, proof of delivery and sign-off, and a 6 inch screen at 2160 x 1080 is enough for that.
  • You want a listed drop rating: the A6 is rated for 1.5 metre drops, and the A8 lists no drop rating.
  • You want the newer operating system: the A6 runs Android 15, the A8 Android 12. Check your own apps on the device either way.

Choose the Tuga A8 if

  • You fill in forms, test schedules or long checklists on site and want 8 inches of screen rather than pinching and zooming on 6.
  • You work on bright roofs and open sites: the A8 is rated at 1000 nits, and the A6 lists no brightness figure.
  • You want the larger battery: 8000mAh against 5050mAh, and both are removable, so a charged spare works on either.
  • You want it on the dashboard: the A8 has VESA mount points and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) is listed for it, the A6 is not.
  • You keep a lot on the device: 6GB of RAM and 128GB of storage against 4GB and 64GB on the A6.

FAQ

Questions about the A6 and A8

If you do not scan, yes. For £30 more the A8 has the 8 inch 1000 nit screen, a larger removable battery (8000mAh against 5050mAh), more RAM and storage, and VESA mounting for the vehicle dock, so for forms, test schedules, checklists, drawings and PDFs it is the better buy. If your work is scanning parcels, stock or asset tags, or you want the device in a pocket, the A6 at £349 is the one: it has the Zebra 2D scan engine the A8 lacks, a 1.5 metre drop rating, Android 15 against Android 12, and it weighs 277g.

Short ones should be fine, but check your own app first. The A6 screen is 6 inches at 2160 x 1080, a pocket-sized screen suited to short job sheets, scans and signatures. Long forms and drawings mean a lot of scrolling, pinching and zooming, which is where the A8 starts to pay for itself. Both use the same Helio P35 processor, and the A6 has 4GB of RAM against the A8's 6GB, so try your heaviest app. Open the longest form you fill in on a typical day and see whether you can work through it one-handed. The Capacitive Stylus (£14.99) is listed for the A8 but not for the A6, which matters if you want a stylus for customer signatures.

Both are sealed to IP67, which covers dust and short immersion, so both are sealed against rain and a drop in a puddle. Beyond that, the A6 has more listed: a 1.5 metre drop rating and an operating range of -20°C to 50°C. The A8 lists no drop rating and no operating temperature, and neither lists MIL-STD-810H, so if a drop or temperature figure matters to you, the A6 is the one with numbers behind it. Our IP rating guide and MIL-STD-810H guide explain what each rating does and does not test.

Not with the same dock. The A8 has VESA mount points and pogo pin contacts, and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), a locking VESA mount with DC power input, is listed for the A8, A10, W8 and W10. It is not listed for the A6. What fits the A6 is the Car Phone Mount (£17), a heavy duty suction cup mount for rugged handhelds, and the 12V DC Car Charger (£26) fits both. The A6 has charging contacts on the body, but no dock or cradle is listed for it. So the A6 can sit in a suction cup mount and charge from the 12V socket, but if you want a locked-in dashboard unit that comes out as the site tablet, that is the A8. Everything is on the accessories page.
